title: Positional Hierarchy
shortDefinition: A priority map showing which positions increase control, reduce risk, and open submissions.

title: Inside Position
shortDefinition: Inside Position means your hand, head, knee, or hip occupies the space between your structure and the opponent’s center, whoever wins this lane controls the direction of movement.

title: Connection Before Control
shortDefinition: You must attach the correct body points before trying to hold or steer the opponent.

title: Control Before Submission
shortDefinition: Submissions become reliable only when the opponent is held where the main escape structure is denied.

title: Frames
shortDefinition: A frame is a bone structure (forearm, shin, knee, bicep) connected to the torso to maintain space, not arm strength to push.

title: Wedges
shortDefinition: A wedge is a body part inserted into space to block the opponent’s rotation or connection.

title: Levers
shortDefinition: A lever uses one segment of the opponent’s body to rotate or disrupt a larger structure.

title: Hooks
shortDefinition: A hook is a leg or foot connection used to lift, pull, hold hip line, or off-balance.

title: Posts
shortDefinition: A post is a temporary support point to keep base, change hips, or stop rotation.

title: Pummeling
shortDefinition: Pummeling is the repeated battle to regain inside lanes with hands, head, knees, or hips.

title: Head Position
shortDefinition: The head is a post, wedge, pressure source, and sensor that organizes the spine.

title: Hip Line vs Shoulder Line
shortDefinition: Hip line and shoulder line are the two rotation axes that decide passes, pins, escapes, and back exposure.

title: Knee Line
shortDefinition: The Knee Line is the boundary that decides whether the leg is controlled in an entanglement or free.

title: Elbow-Knee Connection
shortDefinition: Elbow-Knee Connection closes the space between upper body and hip line to prevent pins and passes.

title: Base and Balance
shortDefinition: Base is the ability to keep center of gravity while staying mobile and reactive.

title: Angle Creation
shortDefinition: Angle Creation changes body or hip position so your force attacks weak structure instead of pushing straight into strength.

title: Pressure Direction
shortDefinition: Effective pressure has a specific direction: diagonal, to far hip, to shoulder line, or down through hip line.

title: Dilemma Attacks
shortDefinition: A dilemma is two or more threats where defending one line exposes another.

title: Failure Response
shortDefinition: Failure Response is the plan for the moment the first technique is blocked.

title: Early Defense vs Late Defense
shortDefinition: Early defense addresses body signals before the position locks; late defense deals with force already applied.

title: Guard Retention Layers
shortDefinition: Guard Retention has 7 layers: distance → feet → knees → frames → hips → shoulders → re-attack. Each layer lost drops you to the next.

title: Wrestle-Up Philosophy
shortDefinition: Wrestle-up turns Guard from a defensive position into a controlled race to come on top.

title: Leg Lock Safety Hierarchy
shortDefinition: The safety order: recognize entanglement, hide heel, protect Knee Line, clear secondary leg, then exit with control.

title: Deliberate Practice
shortDefinition: Deliberate Practice means choosing one small cue, measuring results, and increasing resistance step by step.

title: Positional Rolling
shortDefinition: Positional Rolling starts in a specific situation with clear win and reset conditions.

title: Exposure Before Finish
shortDefinition: Exposure means opening the finish line before applying finishing force, if the path is not clear, it is not time to squeeze.

title: Ride vs Pin vs Submission
shortDefinition: Three different phases: ride to expose the back, pin to stabilize the position, submission to finish.

title: Safe vs Unsafe Rotation
shortDefinition: Safe rotation occurs when Knee Line is free and heel is hidden; unsafe rotation occurs when Knee Line is trapped and heel is exposed.
